# Plates roadmap

Keep your projects moving: shared practices, bounded automation, and a clear view of what needs you. [Working rules](../AGENTS.md) · [Design](design.md) · [Lessons](lessons.md)

**51 of 116 phases built; 52 owe a walk.** Built means implemented and checked; planned is not available.

**Next focus:** [50. A project's isocan canvas shows what Plates improves](phases/50-project-life-on-isocan.md). Move the approved canvas's weekly "Loop across projects" report to one live card. The owner approved this on 2026-10-13. That binding is published by the weekly script, which calls `canvasSync` with its own keys, not by `plates canvas sync`. Three steps, in the reporting workspace, after this work is released there: 1. Change the script's key for that card from a dated one to the fixed key `loop-across-projects`. The title may keep its date. 2. ⚑ The owner, with the inspected isocan `7bb1f4e` build as the approved writer: `plates canvas live --card loop-across-projects` (preview), then the same with `--yes`. No card has that key yet, so nothing is adopted and no re-base is needed; the dated editions stay on the canvas as history. 3. Let one weekly run create the card and the next one edit it in place. Confirm both in the browser, then edit the card as a person and see the next run refuse. Record it as evidence. If `pulse` is also kept in `--card` and that journal has a pulse published before 2026-10-13, its receipt has no recorded metadata: the preview says `unrecorded-metadata` and it needs one `plates canvas rebase --onto <version-id> --yes` after the owner has looked at the card. After that, provision the dedicated GitHub writer using the project-canvas guide and verify night/restart behavior, including a restored pending edit. Scheduled-use evidence (seven nights) is still owed. Do not ask again for the destination, writer or dashboards. (Dated: phase 13 is on or after 2026-11-01.)

Goals are outcomes, not dates. Counts are derived; superseded work is retired, not delivered.

- **0 done when:** A fresh clone of plates passes `npm run check` on GitHub Actions, and `/conduct plates` can read the next phase and its next action from the repo alone.
- **1 done when:** Plates's own practice files are rendered from `practices/<name>/`, and re-rendering them onto plates changes no bytes.
- **18 done when:** `npm run check` fails when the README's verb or practice tables disagree with the live verb registry or `practices/`, and the conduct skill's Record step names README and the agent guide.
- **32 done when:** `roadmap --check` refuses a phase that still holds `plates phase new`'s template text or an empty Done when, Acceptance or Proof; every acceptance box in a new phase names its check (a test, a command, or ⚑ by hand); and the phase template asks for its Real surfaces, each needing one proof in that place.
- **44 done when:** plates's own roadmap runs with lived-in off (its headline counts built, not lived-in), every plates phase whose building is done and whose rest is a walk or time is marked `owes: walk`, and `plates next` names the next buildable phase instead of one waiting on a walk; no phase is built that was not proven.
- **49 done when:** Repeated measurements on the same machine demonstrate faster practice loading or CLI startup, existing command and validation behavior remains tested, and current documentation agrees with the implemented workflows.
- **51 done when:** `plates board` serves a localhost page that sorts every open item by what it waits on (yours, broken, the agent's, time), each "yours" item settles through a plates verb, phases say when they are not yet buildable and whose walk they owe, and the owner has settled a week of walks from the board instead of in chat.
- **55 done when:** `plates test <file> --stalls` names every test that passes plainly and fails when paused at random moments; plates's own tests it names have moved to mock timers or an injected clock, and run with stalls without failing; the timing-hygiene rule requires stall pins for suite-timing files, using mock or injected clocks to make their assertions independent of wall time, instead of a sleep floor; and the practice ships it to the fleet.
- **62 done when:** `plates prove <test> --fix <files>` reverts the fix's files, runs the named test, records that it failed and how, restores the fix, runs it again, and writes the verdict (VERIFIED, NOT WORKING or INCONCLUSIVE) with the failure text into the commit trailer or the phase's evidence; the conduct skill requires it for every `fix:` commit; and plates's own fixes for two weeks carry it.
- **64 done when:** Every rule plates renders into a project's guide names the failure or lesson that made it (a lesson number, an issue, or one sentence); doctor notes a rule without one; a number in a phase's evidence or a research doc carries the date it was measured and, where one exists, the command that re-derives it; and a lint notes a figure with neither.
- **65 done when:** `.plates/plates.json` `"contracts"` maps path patterns to the document to read first; plates's guide block lists them, doctor checks each doc exists, and a pre-edit hook (where the agent supports hooks) names the doc when a matching file is about to change; and a platform-guard lint fails a test that calls a macOS-only (or Windows-only) tool without a platform skip; both on plates and one adopted project.
- **67 done when:** Repeatable CLI measurements distinguish startup, local residual work, subprocesses and observed network boundaries, and a no-emit type check rejects invalid evidence states in selected production modules.
- **68 done when:** Reconciliation reads GitHub PRs with bounded concurrency while preserving deterministic observations and failures, and local timing work is measured and optimized only where evidence supports it.
- **69 done when:** Measured redundant test work is removed without losing distinct behavioral contracts, missing checks found by coverage and history are addressed, and reproducible evidence explains test counts, cost and limits.
- **70 done when:** A session claims a phase before building it, in a way every other session, provider and machine can see with git alone; `plates next` offers only phases that are ready and unclaimed; and the conduct skill claims before it builds.
- **71 done when:** plates counts a PR's review rounds, and past the limit (three by default) `plates review` stops the fix-and-push loop and gives the owner the choice (merge with the rest tracked, split, or close), with each open finding sorted by the merge rule.
- **84 done when:** `plates prove --mutate` applies small mechanical mutations to the lines the fix changed and runs the named test against each; every mutation the test does not catch is reported as a survivor, and the proof's trailer records how many were caught.
- **85 done when:** A seeded, shrinking, zero-dependency property runner lives in `tests/helpers`, and properties over the plan validator, tick merging, claims and front matter run in the gate, each failure reported as its smallest case and the seed that reproduces it.
- **86 done when:** One test runs a night end to end, with a frozen clock, a bare-origin repo, a stubbed GitHub and the fake isocan: the night writes its plan, a climb pass ticks its item, the morning decides, finalizes and sends the brief, and the card is published; the test checks the brief and the card say what happened.
- **87 done when:** The conduct skill has every builder restate the phase's success criteria before it builds, and report in one shape (changes, each acceptance box with its test or why not, the focused test commands the builder ran with their exit codes, decisions the spec left open, what remains), and the conductor's checklist refuses a report missing those exit codes or an acceptance box. The full gate stays the conductor's, run once on the integrated tree, as the skill already says.
- **90 done when:** A builder brief resolves explicitly linked decisions by scope at the source revision, carries their provenance, and refuses contradictory or unavailable required context before dispatch or resume.
- **91 done when:** A locally reviewed shaping record produces non-overwriting phase drafts or robot rubric previews with attributed decisions, named proof and valid dependencies, while changed inputs invalidate approval.

- **4 done when:** `plates adopt` on duo and on cajones produces a pull request a person merges, after which each project's own check passes and its `.plates/plates.json` names the practice version.
- **5 done when:** `plates doctor` reports every managed file and block whose bytes differ from what plates wrote, and for each offers eject, restore, or send-as-lesson — never reverting on its own.
- **6 done when:** A project on practice version N runs `plates update` and gets one pull request that brings it to N+1 through a migration, passes its check, and is idempotent when run again.
- **16 done when:** `plates adopt` on fresh copies of ledger and isocan reports their real gate, their real lessons file and their real phases, installs nothing that duplicates something they already have, and each copy's own gate passes afterwards. ledger's adoption is a PR for the owner; isocan's is a PR prepared for Dimitri.
- **20 done when:** ledger's adoption PR is merged; ledger's own CI is green on it; one real plates-night on ledger has measured it, opened its health PR and drained it; `plates fleet` shows ledger adopted and current; and ledger's CLI never synced or pushed from a plates run.
- **22 done when:** `plates release` moves the practice version only when `practices/` or `migrations/` changed since the last practice release. A plates-side-only release leaves every project current, and `plates fleet update` opens nothing for it.
- **24 done when:** `plates loose-ends` on this Mac lists, for plates and every project in `plates.json` that has a local checkout, each unfinished thing (a chat session, uncommitted files, an unmerged branch or worktree, an open PR, a phase waiting on a person), each with one suggested next move and the commands to take it. Marking an item resume, park or drop keeps it there across runs.
- **28 done when:** Rendering isocan's `docs/loop/` with plates's `scripts/loop.mjs` gives isocan's own `docs/LOOP.md` with only the generated-by line and wording from `.plates/plates.json` `loop` differing, so isocan can take plates's script.
- **29 done when:** isocan can take plates's `renovate.json` without losing a rule, `plates doctor` names every way a lessons table can split, and `plates adopt` calls a project's claude workflow local only when it answers mentions.
- **39 done when:** Every PR plates opens (fleet update, the night's data PR, and the climb and tend PRs when they exist) has a body built by `scripts/plates/pr-body.mjs` with three sections in order (Summary as a picture, Evidence as before and after, Merge danger as a two-way or one-way door with its blast radius), and a real fleet update PR in an adopted project reads that way.
- **41 done when:** `plates review` reads a PR's review threads and comments deterministically; every plates agent that opens or merges a PR (the conductor, fleet update's report, climb, tend) validates each review comment against the code and answers it as fixed (naming the commit), tracked (naming where) or not valid (saying why), closing the thread when settled; the night counts comments left unanswered; and the next fleet release's reviews are all answered. Nothing blocks a merge.
- **42 done when:** On ledger, a Codex PR (a `codex/` branch) opened after the practice is switched on gets a Claude review within its budget: inline comments tagged P1/P2/P3, each about something the code shows, and a summary; Claude never pushes, approves or merges; and the owner has read that review and judged its comments.
- **45 done when:** A project chooses which agent runs each pass in `.plates/plates.json` (`"agents"`, and an `"agent"` on cross-review, climb and tend), Claude and Codex are both adapters held to the same rules by the same tests, a reviewing agent's findings are posted by plates's own step, and on ledger one pass runs on Codex by changing one line, its result read by the owner.
- **46 done when:** plates-cross-review.yml runs the agent (Claude or Codex) in a job whose token can only read, with no OIDC App token, and posts the review from a second job that runs no agent and nothing from the PR's branch; the workflows test holds that for both providers, and a real review on ledger posts its findings as before.
- **48 done when:** `plates release` refuses while a shipped practice change since the last release has not come through a plates PR reviewed by a provider other than its author with every comment answered, and three releases have gone through that gate; the owner has compared the fleet rounds' findings after it with the eight rounds before.
- **52 done when:** `plates fleet update` never ends a project at FAILED for its check: when the check fails after the update it pushes the branch and opens the PR, ordinary when main fails the same check without the update and a draft otherwise, each opening with what failed; the board lists a draft update PR under Broken; and one real update that failed a project's check has been fixed by a commit on its own branch.
- **53 done when:** `plates release` rehearses the update on every managed fleet project before it commits and tags, and refuses while a project's check passes on main and fails with the release, unless the owner records why; three releases have gone through it, and the owner has compared their fleet rounds with v0.8.23 to v0.8.26.
- **58 done when:** `plates adopt` on a project whose guide is CLAUDE.md (and no AGENTS.md) turns lessons and night on, with plates's blocks in CLAUDE.md, and creates no AGENTS.md; render, doctor and update treat that guide as they treat AGENTS.md; and one real project adopted this way keeps a single guide.
- **60 done when:** On a project with `"crossReview": { "after": "push" }`, every push to main is reviewed by a provider other than its author, as one batch; each finding is posted where the owner reads it, answered fixed, tracked or not valid like any other, and a tracked one is a `keel:agent` issue; nothing about the push waits on it; and a month of one real project's pushes has been reviewed.
- **63 done when:** On a project with `"phases": { "source": "milestones" }`, `plates next`, the board and the night read its open GitHub milestones as phases (the milestone's description as Done when, its issues as acceptance boxes, its deadline as `due`, without postponing work, closed when the milestone closes); nothing is written into the project's plans; and one real project's plan shows on the board this way for a release.
- **109 done when:** Plates runs under its new product, repository, executable and configuration names across the verified collection, with production serving the checked revision and existing data, permissions and unrelated work preserved.
- **112 done when:** Ledger core and web start independently after scope resolution with the existing stage coverage, clocks and failure propagation preserved.
- **113 done when:** A stalled isocan installation fails within its configured bound with redacted diagnostics and any targeted retry retains immutable inputs and attempt history.

- **10 done when:** Plates and one adopted project each run `plates-night.yml` nightly for a week, each night leaving at most one open machine PR, with Renovate's lanes active and a red run reaching the owner by email.
- **11 done when:** `plates improve` writes `docs/health/<date>.md` with deterministic measures and one proposal, changes nothing else, and its self-test fails on a fixture built to be unhealthy.
- **14 done when:** One adopted project's Loop cycle (pull new insights, propose a rank for each, render `docs/LOOP.md`) runs through plates's `loop` practice, and that project's own scripts/loop.* is retired in favour of it.
- **15 done when:** A project made by `plates init` runs its night shift with no plates checkout and no `PLATES_TOKEN`, and the update PR a project receives is opened from plates by `plates fleet update`.
- **26 done when:** Plates's existing checks detect and propose scoped corrections for merged-PR, completed-next-action and superseded-decision contradictions on an adopted project, without inferring acceptance, production verification or lived-in status from a merge.
- **27 done when:** `plates improve` on a projects-shaped repo (isocan) reports `phases_stuck`, `phases_without_issue` and the new record measures with values, not `n/a`, and every new measure is `n/a` with a reason, never a zero, where the project has nothing for it to read.
- **33 done when:** After `npm test` in plates and in one adopted project, the run ends with a hygiene block naming any test that was flaky or got slower over its last N runs, with the command to reproduce it; the night's health page counts both; and one real hygiene item has been found and fixed this way.
- **35 done when:** A project that opts in (plates first) gets, on a scheduled night, one `keel-climb/test-time/<date>` PR made by an agent under the shared protocol: a baseline, kept changes each with numbers measured against noise, a list of what was tried and reverted, the gate green; or, when nothing beat the noise, no PR and a line on the health page saying so. Nothing it opens merges without a person.
- **36 done when:** A climb night picks `hygiene` when the ledger names a flaky test and opens a PR that makes it pass reliably (its fix shown by the ledger over repeated runs on one clean tree) or files an issue saying why it could not; and a project that names a `build` command gets `build-time` PRs under the same protocol.
- **37 done when:** On ledger, climb nights have run each of `perf` (its own benchmark command, measured under the protocol), `lessons` (a distill pass over ledger's table, proposals for the owner) and `loop` (Loop's new findings pulled and each given a proposed rank), each opening at most one PR that the owner reads, and none deciding anything a person decides.
- **38 done when:** On plates and one adopted project, a scheduled tend pass has read the night's record findings and opened one `keel-tend/<date>` PR that resolves them (corrections applied, lost proofs repaired or proposed back to partial, docs brought in line, drift and loose ends described for the owner to choose), the owner has merged it, and the next night's record findings fell to what the PR left, each of those named on the health page with what was tried.
- **43 done when:** plates's health page shows a Budget line for tend and climb: the agent step's minutes in each of the last runs (at most 8), which ran out, and a suggestion (extend, shorten to N, hold, or too few to say), read from GitHub's record of the runs; and the owner has read tend's line and kept or changed its budget by it.
- **47 done when:** A project can set `"agent": "codex"` on climb and on tend, and one Codex climb night and one Codex tend pass have run on a project under the unchanged three-job sandbox and guard, each PR read by the owner; Codex never runs with `danger-full-access` or `unsafe`.
- **54 done when:** An issue labelled `keel:agent` that meets the rubric is worked by an agent with no person starting it: a PR through climb's sandbox, reviewed by the other provider, the agent's last message posted on the issue, and the owner's comment starting the next run; on a project with the pass turned on and a budget set, three such issues have been merged.
- **57 done when:** The night measures time against bounds (`gate_time`, `time_creep`, `wall_clock_tests`, `inconclusive_share`, `critical_file`; `worked_around` from the conductor's machine), its proposal names the fix when one is outside, an accepted time proposal is filed as a `keel:agent` issue that the robot builds, and two such fixes have been merged and their measure seen back inside its bound.
- **59 done when:** A project whose tests run on `bun test` or vitest gets the same ledger records as one on `node --test` (each top-level test's file, name, outcome and time, with the run's commit, tree, machine and config), and `flaky_tests` and `slow_tests` work on it; one real project on each runner has a week of records.
- **66 done when:** The night measures stale worktrees (merged into main or untouched for a week, with the disk they hold), draft PRs waiting longer than a bound, and source files longer than a bound in lines; each outside its bound names its fix (the worktrees to remove, the PRs to finish, the file to split and where); and one fix from each has been proposed and taken.
- **73 done when:** Every night has one plan file, written before any pass runs (plates's default plan when the owner did not shape it), every pass that runs that night ticks its item with an outcome, and the health page shows the plan and what became of each item.
- **74 done when:** The owner can say what tonight is for: `plates goodnight` (and the conduct practice's `/goodnight` skill, which runs it in conversation) shows what was settled today, what was left open, the default plan and a few things to try, takes the owner's changes, and on `--yes` writes the plan the night then runs.
- **75 done when:** A project can declare personas in `.agents/personas/<name>.md`, each with goals that are numbers it measures with its own command, and `plates persona run` measures every goal, writes a dated review page, and turns each missed goal into a candidate item for the next night's default plan.
- **76 done when:** Each build item in tonight's plan is handed to a pass that already builds safely (a climb job, or a robot issue), names the number it moves before the work starts, respects the plan's "will not touch" list, and ticks its item with the PR it opened or the reason it failed; nothing builds that the plan does not name.
- **77 done when:** With a canvas, tonight's plan is a live card updated in place as items tick; and every morning `plates morning` writes the brief in isocan's order (done, tried, failed, left alone) with links to the canvas, the health page and each PR, delivered as a GitHub issue assigned to the owner so that GitHub emails it.
- **78 done when:** Through a night, the canvas plan card shows each item's latest status after every pass finishes, with no one at a keyboard; a night that ran plates's default plan records its outcomes exactly as an owner's plan does; and an accepted Loop finding the owner adds to tonight's plan is built by the robot under its rubric, never left in a lane no pass builds.
- **88 done when:** Configured fleet projects collect bounded production error evidence into the existing night practice, deduplicate recurring errors into reviewable repair work, and distinguish deployed verified fixes from missing evidence while preserving source acceptance.
- **89 done when:** An opted-in project reuses successful exact-revision CI gate evidence beyond 24 hours while changed, dirty, failed or unavailable evidence still causes a real gate and time-dependent night work continues.
- **92 done when:** Feedback retains the exact reviewed result and proposes a deduplicated follow-up with fresh routing facts, without publishing private words, accepting decisions or starting work automatically.
- **114 done when:** Consumer configured-gate reuse is accepted only from complete exact-head equivalent stage evidence and adversarial invalidation tests reject unsupported reuse.

The owner's two-sessions walk waits. · [#166](https://github.com/dalmaer/plates/issues/166) |

- **79 done when:** Each commit's gate runs once in CI and its result and test-ledger runs are kept; every plates pass (night, loop, climb, tend, robot judges) and the pre-push hook reuse an exact, clean result for the commit they would test and run the gate only when there is none; and a change that touches only documentation skips the suite.
- **80 done when:** Many commits test at once, but one queued publisher advances a tested ref (`green` by default) only for the newest commit whose gate passed, skips any commit a later one has already passed, and refuses a ref that has diverged; deploys follow the tested ref, never `main`; and every installed workflow cancels superseded test runs and never cancels a deploy, which a workflow test checks.
- **81 done when:** A deploy is skipped when production already serves the commit or a descendant; after a deploy, plates waits until production reports the deployed commit (or a descendant) at the project's version endpoint and passes its smoke checks; and a failure reaches the owner once, in the morning issue and on the board.
- **82 done when:** `plates promote [<commit>]` moves a project's production ref only to a commit on its tested ref, previews first, verifies production serves it afterwards (phase 81), and `plates promote --back <commit>` rolls back the same way; it is always a person's command and nothing runs it automatically.
- **83 done when:** A session that finishes a change runs only its fast checks and marks it ready instead of running the full gate and pushing; one integrator, holding a claim-based lock, takes every ready change as a batch, runs the full gate once on the combined tree and pushes it; and a failing batch is split until the change that broke it is found and sent back, while the rest land.

## G7 — Operate every Plates project from a private web workspace

From mobile and desktop, an authenticated owner operates every authorized Plates project: decisions, guided tests, visual changes, routine history and execution, fleet lessons and updates, scoped credentials and policy-bound model capacity, with source-backed evidence and private data.

- **93 done when:** An explicitly configured external workspace can be inspected and initialized from the installed CLI without writing private data into application or project Git trees.
- **94 done when:** The owner has an approved deployment recipe and verified private workspace repository, host and selected-repository GitHub App binding, with credentials stored only in the deployment secret store.
- **95 done when:** The deployed service authenticates its owner and denies every project, artifact and operation outside the current user, workspace and installation intersection.
- **96 done when:** Authenticated Home shows decisions, ready walks, recent additions and project summaries that remain truthful and usable through incremental refresh and incomplete source reads.
- **97 done when:** An owner can review and record a decision against exact current source facts and recover its operation receipt without accepting recommendations or duplicating uncertain writes.
- **98 done when:** An owner can test an exact result step by step, resume private observations and explicitly accept a successful walk while failed, blocked or stale tests leave acceptance open.
- **99 done when:** Recent additions show authorized real captures, precise availability and links to the corresponding tested revision and guided walk without leaking private artifacts.
- **100 done when:** The owner can inspect daily work and shared lessons, migrate selected workspace records and explicitly export approved material while retaining project authority and existing budgets.
- **101 done when:** The owner repeatedly uses the hosted workspace across real projects and a restore exercise preserves private records and access boundaries without falsely completing work.
- **102 done when:** The owner can inspect routine definitions and all observed attempts across authorized projects, with source coverage, outcomes, evidence and costs visible in both fleet and project views.
- **103 done when:** The owner can configure scoped provider credentials and inspect supported account/model capacity with source freshness, shared-pool identity and explicit unsupported coverage.
- **104 done when:** The owner can start, cancel, retry and manage supported routines from the web with durable receipts, bounded budgets and no duplicate effects after disconnect or worker failure.
- **105 done when:** The owner can compare fleet versions, preview and launch selected update PRs, and trace a lesson from its source through release to observed project adoption.
- **106 done when:** Each run selects an eligible model under an explicit capacity and budget policy, explains the choice and preserves task and review requirements during fallback or handoff.
- **107 done when:** Every current Plates operation has a deliberate web treatment, and core fleet/project journeys work on mobile and desktop without a terminal detour.
- **108 done when:** Repeated real use demonstrates that the owner operates the selected fleet from mobile and desktop, including routine failure recovery, updates, learning and bounded model fallback.

## Updating this roadmap

Edit the [phase](phases/README.md), its acceptance and evidence, then `npm run roadmap` and `npm run check`. CI checks metadata, the dependency graph, evidence links and that this file is current; it cannot check that a claim is true.
